relevance.rationale: The corpus asserts, in rem:quantum-bloch-group-framework-connection, that 'the regulator map B(q) -> R sends the algebraic volume to the hyperbolic volume' -- an unsourced claim in a remark block. This paper is the rigorous version of that statement on the A-polynomial curve: it uses the Beilinson-Deligne regulator to show the symbol {l,m} in K_2(C(Y)) is torsion for every component Y of the A-polynomial zero locus of a hyperbolic knot, and derives a quantization of the Chern-Simons period. Supporting rather than core because QOU's Bloch-group content is q-deformed and Hecke-traced, and no QOU number is computed from Li-Wang; the paper supplies the classical statement the q-deformed one is modelled on.

keyResults.statement: The closed real 1-form eta(l,m) = log|l| d arg m - log|m| d arg l is EXACT on Y_h; and for any loop gamma in Y_h, (1/4pi^2) times the integral of (log|m| d log|l| + arg l d arg m) equals k/N where N is the ORDER of the symbol {l,m} in K_2(C(Y)).
keyResults.useForFolio: Makes rigorous the corpus's 'regulator sends algebraic volume to hyperbolic volume' assertion, and supplies the quantization statement that docs/scope/2026-07-12-mq0-unified-boundary-selection.md gestures at ('a quantization condition' on the Im V = 0 locus) with no source. The torsion order N is a concrete arithmetic invariant of the A-polynomial curve that the folio's regulator language currently lacks.

keyResults.statement: The class r(l,m) in H^1(Y_h, C*) is a flat line bundle -- the pullback of the universal Heisenberg line bundle over C* x C* -- and the derived 1-form is its Chern-Simons secondary class; the generalized volume conjecture is reformulated via this 1-form.
keyResults.useForFolio: Gives the A-polynomial curve a K-theoretic/line-bundle structure, which is the classical shadow of what the folio calls the quantum Bloch group. Cite where def:quantum-bloch-group motivates the regulator.
